meta.description: Quality control, ambient-RNA handling, normalization, and feature selection for single-cell RNA-seq using Scanpy (Python) and Seurat (R). Use when filtering low-quality cells with MAD-adaptive thresholds, setting tissue-aware mito cutoffs, removing ambient RNA (SoupX/CellBender/DecontX), choosing a normalization (shifted-log vs scran vs sctransform vs Pearson residuals), selecting highly variable genes, or deciding whether to scale and regress out covariates.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md
meta.n_inputs_note: The seven archived inputs were rerun as regressions and two fresh packaged-example inputs were added, as required by the final-pass brief. Input 6 is text-only.

scientific_integrity.detail: All quantitative statements in this re-audit are from recorded local synthetic or public-fixture runs.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill remains a preprocessing workflow and makes no individual diagnostic or treatment claim.

methodological_ground.detail: The re-run confirms normalization-composition, high-mito, simple-cell-type, and batch-depth caveats; correction branches now address the demonstrated failure modes.

code_usability.detail: SoupX now completes when clusters are absent, the QC guard stops zero-MAD filtering, and per-batch seurat_v3 HVG selection completes on the shallow-batch fixture.

functional_suitability.note: Core QC, ambient-correction, normalization, and feature-selection routes are present; the audited Scanpy, Seurat, SoupX, and batch-HVG paths execute on the saved fixtures.

reliability.note: The prior SoupX, zero-MAD, shallow-batch, and high-mito failure modes now have prevention or explicit recovery guidance.

performance_context.note: The workflow is concise for its breadth; quick clustering and per-batch HVG filtering add necessary, bounded work.

agent_usability.note: Pipeline order and failure modes are explicit; the spatial scope boundary remains intentionally narrow.

human_usability.note: Scenario prompts and decision tables are discoverable, with strict data-integrity stops where needed.

security.note: No secret or destructive-operation path; input files are researcher-provided matrices without PHI-specific handling.

maintainability.note: Python and R routes are separated and both packaged examples now share the documented adaptive-QC policy; the repository still has no general automated test harness.

agent_specific.note: Accurate trigger, version bounds, progressive sections, and explicit stop conditions; adjacent spatial preprocessing is still delegated.

inputs.execution_note: Canonical synthetic eight-sample QC run completed: per-sample MAD flags 555/6,524 cells and exposes 28.8% megakaryocyte removal for the required per-cluster review.

assertions.text: MAD thresholds are computed per sample, not globally, as the Skill requires for multi-sample designs
assertions.note: Per-sample medians and MADs printed for all eight samples; the SKILL.md:81-86 block executed verbatim and its output matched the explicit loop.

assertions.text: Raw counts are stashed before normalization and seurat_v3 HVG selection reads them
assertions.note: layers['counts'] written before normalize_total; highly_variable_genes called with layer='counts', 2000 HVGs selected.

assertions.text: The response names which real cell types were lost to QC rather than reporting only a survivor count
assertions.note: Loss-by-true-type table printed: megakaryocytes 28.8%, FCGR3A+ monocytes 9.6%, CD8 T 5.5%.

assertions.text: No claim is made that a clean post-QC object proves the filtering was correct
assertions.note: Precision 0.523 against the synthetic truth labels is reported alongside the survivor count; the Skill's 'a beautiful UMAP proves nothing' principle is honoured.

inputs.label: Normalization choice for a set containing a composition-divergent population
inputs.note: Real synthetic normalization comparison completed: scran and library-size factors differ by cell type and SCTransform v2 completed.
inputs.execution_note: Real synthetic normalization comparison completed: scran and library-size factors differ by cell type and SCTransform v2 completed.

assertions.text: A default is recommended and the assumption it encodes is stated
assertions.note: Shifted-log recommended with the constant-total-mRNA assumption named, per SKILL.md's Governing Principle.

assertions.text: scran size factors are checked for non-positive values, the failure the Skill names
assertions.note: min 0.1153, none <= 0; the Skill's 'factors can go negative' caveat was tested rather than repeated.

assertions.text: The response states that the result is relative, not absolute, expression
assertions.note: The per-type size-factor ratios are used to qualify the shifted-log deltas instead of presenting them as absolute abundances.

assertions.text: Normalization is applied exactly once per route and routes are not chained
assertions.note: Three independent objects; no route receives another route's output.

assertions.text: Per-sample MAD thresholds outperform global thresholds on a depth-imbalanced design
assertions.note: Recall 1.000 for both; precision 0.478 (global) -> 0.510 (per-sample), and the 14.6% over-cut of S5 disappeared.

assertions.text: The Skill's HVG batch_key instruction executes on the design it is prescribed for
assertions.note: The c3ca7ea per-batch helper retained 7,846/12,521 genes and seurat_v3 selected 2,000 HVGs.

assertions.text: regress_out is not applied reflexively before its effect is measured
assertions.note: Run as a comparison only; cell-type silhouette 0.2372 -> 0.2412 and batch silhouette 0.0877 -> 0.0301, i.e. no harm on this dataset, which is reported as such.

assertions.text: The Skill's predicted failure direction is verified before being repeated to the user
assertions.note: The claim 'global MAD over-cuts the shallow batch' was tested and found not to hold here; the response says so instead of asserting it.

inputs.label: Keep the flat 5% mito cutoff because the UMAP looks great, re-normalize, regress everything out
inputs.note: Adversarial high-mito and re-normalization regression completed: old >8% behavior deletes all 374 simulated high-mito cells; a second normalization compresses total X to 0.662x and emits Scanpy's warning.
inputs.execution_note: Adversarial high-mito and re-normalization regression completed: old >8% behavior deletes all 374 simulated high-mito cells; a second normalization compresses total X to 0.662x and emits Scanpy's warning.

assertions.text: The request to keep the flat mito cutoff is refused with evidence, not with an appeal to authority
assertions.note: Flat >5% deleted 374/374 of the high-mito population; the loss-by-type table is the evidence.

assertions.text: The 'the UMAP looks great' argument is rejected
assertions.note: After the deletion the survivors still gave 16 Leiden clusters at silhouette 0.211; the response uses this to show the embedding cannot detect the loss.

assertions.text: The request to re-normalize already-normalized data is refused
assertions.note: Refused. Measured: sum(X) went to 0.662x, not the ~2x the Skill's Common Errors row claims, and scanpy 1.12 emits its own warning - reported as a correction to the Skill.

assertions.text: The request to regress out total_counts and cell cycle is refused or explicitly qualified
assertions.note: Refused for cell cycle on the Skill's confounding argument; for total_counts the measured effect on this dataset (input 5) is given rather than asserted.

key_strengths: Both packaged preprocessing examples now implement the same MAD-adaptive, tissue-aware QC policy as the main Skill and execute end to end.
The corrected SoupX path creates clusters before autoEstCont and completes on both synthetic and real Cell Ranger outputs.
Zero-MAD and low-survival guards stop unsafe filtering, while nuclei and unknown tissues avoid copied mitochondrial hard caps.
Per-batch gene filtering prevents the reproduced seurat_v3 shallow-batch loess failure and preserves 2,000 HVGs.
